name: Claim Ledger Protocol — consumption log
why: The protocol asks sites to publish /claimledger.json. This file publishes whether anyone actually reads it, including when the answer is nobody. 'Ledgers published' is deliberately NOT reported as traction: llms.txt scored well on exactly that number while being dead.

definitions.ledgers_listed: Ledgers on the reference registry, first-party included.
definitions.ledgers_validating: Of those, how many parse and carry all five required fields in every entry.
definitions.outside_fetches_of_our_claimledger: Fetches of goldrush.agiscorecard.com/claimledger.json by a client this network did NOT write. Excluded, all three: (a) any fetch carrying a goldrush referrer — our own registry page fetches the file; (b) our deployment self-check, which tags itself ?ci=1; (c) fetches made by our own agiscorecard MCP server's get_claim_ledger tool, which is our code calling our file. Exclusion (c) was added 2026-08-31 after exactly that happened on 2026-08-30 and would otherwise have counted as adoption on the first day the number was published — the failure mode this file exists to prevent.
definitions.known_limit: An external ledger's own readership is unobservable from here. The 2026-11-30 adoption line is therefore resolved by this number plus registry ledger_render events whose label is a non-goldrush URL.

note: Two self-inflicted signals caught and excluded so far. (1) Ten machine fetches of /ledger.json were this repository's own deploy self-check — ten deploys, ten fetches. (2) One fetch of /claimledger.json on 2026-08-30 was our own MCP server's get_claim_ledger tool. Neither is adoption. The count stays 0.
